Chi-square test of a categorical column against a known distribution

Source: R/drift.R
drftchisq.Rd

Tests whether the category counts of a new sample agree with a reference distribution taken as known (proportions fixed by a specification, or a published breakdown): Pearson's chi-square goodness-of-fit test. When the reference is itself a sample, use drfthomog(), which carries the reference's own sampling error.

Usage

drftchisq(obs, expd)

Arguments

obs

Named counts of the new sample, or a factor or text to be tabulated.

expd

Named reference counts or proportions, or a factor or text to be tabulated; rescaled to the total of obs.

Value

A named numeric vector of class drftchisq: statistic, df, p_value and logpvalue (the log of the upper tail, which keeps its information where p_value underflows), with the inputs in the attribute lakner.

Details

Categories present in one argument and not the other are aligned by name, so a vanished category registers as a shortfall. With \(O_j\) the observed counts and \(E_j = N e_j / \sum e\) the reference scaled to the observed total, $$X^2 = \sum_j \frac{(O_j - E_j)^2}{E_j}$$ over the categories with \(E_j > 0\), on \(k - 1\) degrees of freedom; the p-value is the upper tail, computed directly. A category that occurs but which the reference gives probability zero contradicts it outright: statistic is then Inf and p_value 0. With a single category there is nothing to test: df is 0 and the p-values NA. The approximation is poor below expected counts of about 5.

See also

drfthomog(), stats::chisq.test().

Examples

ref <- c(a = 50, b = 30, c = 20)
drftchisq(c(a = 100, b = 60, c = 40), ref)
#> drftchisq: statistic = 0, df = 2, p_value = 1, logpvalue = 0 
#> inputs: n = 200, k = 3 
drftchisq(c(a = 40, b = 60, c = 100), ref)
#> drftchisq: statistic =  1.26e+02, df =  2.00e+00, p_value =  4.36e-28, logpvalue = -6.30e+01 
#> inputs: n = 200, k = 3 
drftchisq(c("a", "a", "b", "b"), c("a", "b"))
#> drftchisq: statistic = 0, df = 1, p_value = 1, logpvalue = 0 
#> inputs: n = 4, k = 2 
drftchisq(c("a", "a", "b", "d"), c("a", "a", "b", "b"))
#> drftchisq: statistic =  Inf, df =    1, p_value =    0, logpvalue = -Inf 
#> inputs: n = 4, k = 3
